gap: No result ChatGPT got works out evenings per charge or price per rated hour for these headsets. Using maker prices read on 2026-11-08, the EKSA E900WT costs $39.99 for 80 rated hours with the lights off: $0.50 per rated hour, or about 26 three-hour evenings per charge. The Logitech G435 costs $79.99 for 18 hours: $4.44 per hour, or 6 evenings. The HyperX Cloud Jet costs $79.99 for 25 hours: $3.20 per hour, or about 8 evenings.
standout_why: I opened the cited SoundGuys page. It gives Amazon and MSRP prices plus the G435's measured battery figure ('over 24 hours in testing') and the Arctis 1's '25-hour battery life'. It gives no price per hour and no evenings per charge, and it has no EKSA, Cloud Jet or G321. Gamecuki was not cited. It lists rated hours (Cloud Jet up to 25 h; EKSA E900WT 80 h lights off, 30 h lights on) but no prices ('all under $50 at the time of writing') and no derived figures. Some of the cited rival pages could not be read. The two cited RTINGS pages came back as navigation only (no picks or figures). Vaagame failed with a TLS certificate error. PC Gamer's guide and its G321 review came back as titles only. So I cannot rule out that RTINGS or Vaagame print a figure like this, which is why this scores 2 rather than 3.
decides: At maker stores today, none of the three brand-name picks ChatGPT gave is under $50. The Logitech G435 and HyperX Cloud Jet are $79.99, and the Logitech G321 is $54.99 (on sale from $59.99). ChatGPT's $39.99 Cloud Jet price came from Best Buy, which I could not verify. That leaves EKSA as the only maker-priced options under $50. The derived figures put the E900WT first on endurance per dollar ($0.50/h, 80 h lights off). The E1000 WT ($35.99, 36 h) and E900 BT ($49.99, 50 h) both come to $1.00/h. Two limits on that: the E900WT is not in Dealectric's product list, and its 80 h is a lights-off claim with no mode named (30 h with LEDs on, about 10 evenings). The E900 BT keeps its place because it is the only one of the three with a 3.5 mm cable for Xbox. The E1000 WT is the strongest for a quick top-up: EKSA rates 10 minutes of charging at 3 hours of play, enough for one 3-hour evening.
